title: Mortal repentance must be perfectly practical cessation; venial repentance cannot be
source_text: XLV. Tertio denique, quia poenitentia ad peccatorum mortalium remissionem, & ad salutem eorum qui ea committunt necessaria debet esse perfecte practica, hoc est, exire debet in realem & actualem ab omnibus hujus generis peccatis cessationem, ut videre est Prov. 28. 13. Joh. 5. 14. Nam si aliquis uno aut altero peccato mor-tali relicto, in alia subinde labatur, is neque gratiam in hac vita, nec gloriam in futura consequi poterit, ut docet Apostolus 1 Cor. 6. 9, 10. Galat. 5. 21. Contra vero poenitentia ad venialium peccatorum remissionem requisita, nec est, nec esse potest perfecte practica, quoad hujus generis peccata. Nam ut omnes fatentur, nemo sine hujus generis peccatis vivere potest: & per consequens, non periclitatur piorum salus, etsi ante finem vitae non possint hoc peccati genus effugere.
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly finally, because the repentance necessary for the remission of mortal sins and for the salvation of those who commit them ought to be perfectly practical—that is, it ought to issue in real and actual cessation from all sins of this kind, as is to be seen in Prov. 28:13 and John 5:14. For if someone, having left one or another mortal sin, presently falls into others, he will be able to obtain neither grace in this life nor glory in the future, as the Apostle teaches in 1 Cor. 6:9–10 and Gal. 5:21. But on the contrary the repentance required for remission of venial sins neither is nor can be perfectly practical as regards sins of this kind. For as all confess, no one can live without sins of this kind: and consequently the salvation of the pious is not endangered even if before the end of life they cannot escape this kind of sin.
pass_b_english: Mortal repentance must actually quit the whole class—or grace and glory are lost (Paul’s vice-lists).
Venial repentance cannot be ‘perfectly practical’ in that sense: no one lives without such faults, yet the godly are not thereby damned.

choices.why: Class-cessation for mortal; impossibility for venial daily faults.
